units.requirement: A conventional alpha-beta TCR recognizes a peptide together with its displaying HLA molecule; this is a combined recognition surface, not a universal description of every nonconventional T-cell receptor.
HLA holds the peptide in its groove; the TCR contacts that displayed surface. The cartoon does not place the peptide in an independent TCR peptide pocket.

The alpha and beta recognition chains both contribute variable and constant regions. Variable domains lie at the contact face and constant domains nearer the T-cell membrane; the chain pairing matters.

CDR3 spans receptor gene-segment junctions generated during V(D)J recombination and is highly variable. CDR3 loops from both chains and other contact regions contribute; CDR3 alone is not a complete specificity code.
Beta-only sequence or a shared CDR3 grouping is less complete than paired alpha-beta identity, and even a complete paired identity does not itself establish receptor antigen, function or safety.

Associated CD3 signaling proteins have a different job from the alpha-beta recognition surface. Signal transmission and supporting cellular context connect recognition to a response; contact is not an automatic killing instruction.

Experiments show cross-reactivity across peptide/HLA contexts for particular TCRs, but this does not establish that an arbitrary TCR recognizes every HLA allele or provide a universal cross-reactivity rate.
A stronger binder is not automatically safer. A schematic contact or one positive recognition test is not exhaustive healthy-tissue, cross-reactivity or safety testing.

Receptor sequence and abundance measurements do not by themselves name the target or establish natural tumor presentation. A sampled molecular identity is distinct from a functional recognition experiment.
Peptide-HLA multimer binding, stimulation/activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit are different endpoints and require evidence appropriate to each claim.

Controlled recognition and killing comparisons need irrelevant targets, appropriate HLA controls and target-only viability controls. Peptide-loaded test cells can bypass natural antigen-processing/presentation steps.

In the fictional example, one beta chain is shared by two cells with different alpha partners and only one reconstructed pair responds to a peptide-loaded target. This does not establish the second pair response, natural untreated tumor recognition or killing by both original cells.

Vaccination can activate or expand mature cells with receptors generated before the encounter and does not normally rewrite mature TCRs; engineered TCR therapy introduces selected receptor sequences. These routes still require natural tumor display, useful function and healthy-tissue safety evidence.

The recognition chain, CD3 signaling complex and response-supporting context are separate components; the diagram locates qualitative domains and loops rather than measuring binding energies, atomic contacts, a full stoichiometric assembly or patient outcome.
